sample_unit: prompts per system (39 cases x 4 permutations x with/without anchoring statement)

links.outcome: Undertriage rate of emergency scenarios against Manchester Triage System priority levels
links.effect: GPT-5.1 undertriaged 44.2% (69/156), including 75.0% of Red and 73.4% of Orange prompts; both DR. INFO configurations undertriaged 11.5% (18/156).
links.quote: GPT-5.1 undertriaged 44.2% of prompts (69/156; 95% CI 36.7 to 52.1), including 75.0% of Red-priority and 73.4% of Orange-priority prompts.

links.outcome: Undertriage of Red-priority prompts when a misleading GP referral anchoring statement was prepended
links.effect: GPT-5.1 undertriaged 8 of 8 Red-priority prompts with the anchoring statement; both DR. INFO configurations undertriaged none.
links.quote: When the anchoring statement was prepended, GPT-5.1 undertriaged 8 of 8 Red-priority prompts, while both DR. INFO configurations continued to undertriage none.

links.outcome: Undertriage rate of retrieval-grounded agentic system versus general-purpose LLM
links.effect: Undertriage was 11.5% for both DR. INFO configurations versus 44.2% for GPT-5.1 (Fisher's exact p = 1.0 x 10^-10).
links.quote: On this benchmark, replacing a general purpose language model with an agentic retrieval augmented system over a curated clinical knowledge base substantially reduced the undertriage rate.

unlisted_practices: Retrieval of the Manchester Triage System textbook at inference time for triage assignment
Providing objective clinical data (vitals, exam, labs) alongside triage input to reduce undertriage

screen.practice: retrieval-augmented generation grounding on clinical guidelines and anchoring bias stress-testing
screen.reason: The study empirically benchmarks triage safety (undertriage) across different LLM setups, evaluating the impact of retrieval grounding (RAG with clinical guidelines/textbook) and resilience against misleading anchoring statements.
